question: In erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py, what is the difference in behavior between BudgetValidation's "Stop" and "Warn" budget actions?
expected_key_facts: erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py, the BudgetValidation.execute_action method
"Stop" calls self.stop(), which raises a BudgetError via frappe.throw - blocks the transaction
"Warn" calls self.warn(), which shows a frappe.msgprint message - does not block
rationale: Verified by reading budget_controller.py directly: stop() (line 292) calls frappe.throw(msg, BudgetError, ...); warn() (line 295) calls frappe.msgprint(...); execute_action() (line 298) branches on the action string to call one or the other.

question: In ERPNext's budget enforcement (erpnext/controllers/budget_controller.py), what lets a user bypass a "Stop" budget action and get only a warning instead?
expected_key_facts: holding the role named in self.exception_approver_role (an Exception Approver Role configured on the Budget)
checked via frappe.get_roles(frappe.session.user) inside BudgetValidation.execute_action
rationale: Verified in budget_controller.py's execute_action method (lines 298-303): if self.exception_approver_role is set and is among frappe.get_roles(frappe.session.user), it calls self.warn(msg) and returns immediately, before the Stop/Warn branch that would otherwise raise.
